cases.prompt: Position our Acme team software against Beta and Gamma for a US team of 10 users buying one year. SSO and export matter. Compare evidence fairly as of 2030-04-10; two competitors suffice.

sources.title: Acme pricing
sources.content: Acme is $10 per user per month, annual commitment. SSO and export are included in this plan. Current 2030-04-10.

sources.title: Beta pricing
sources.content: Beta is $80 per workspace per month, includes 10 users, annual commitment. SSO requires a mandatory $40 per workspace per month add-on. Export is not mentioned. Current 2030-04-10.

sources.title: Gamma pricing
sources.content: Gamma is $8 per user per month annually. Export is available. SSO is announced for next year and is not yet available. Current 2030-04-10.

rubric.description: Marks Beta export unknown and Gamma SSO announced/not currently shipped; does not invent competitor weaknesses from missing docs.
Compares Acme $1200/year, Beta $1440/year including SSO, and Gamma $960/year with its SSO limitation; states the 10-user annual basis.

cases.prompt: Map the market for underwater enterprise CRMs in North America and assess the opportunity as of 2030-04-10.

sources.title: Market survey
sources.content: No underwater-specific enterprise CRM sellers were identified. Only three hobbyists requested such a product; none agreed to pay. Underwater communications reliability makes delivery feasibility unresolved.

sources.title: Global CRM estimate
sources.content: Global CRM software revenue: $100 billion in 2029. Includes all industries and company sizes; vendor revenue survey.

sources.title: North American enterprise estimate
sources.content: North American enterprise CRM implementation services: $20 billion in 2028. Services only; sampled consulting firms, excluding software revenue.

rubric.description: Does not call the empty category demonstrated demand; labels it unproven and identifies willingness-to-pay and feasibility validation.
Keeps global software revenue and regional implementation services estimates separate, preserving geography, year and methodology rather than adding them.
Uses only defensible market segmentation or axes; does not fabricate a populated 2x2 map.
